analysis:
Integration pass over all 37 units. The PR is mostly docs plus tests and golden fixtures. The runtime changes visible in the supplied evidence are in Gemma4StageGeometry, Gemma4PlacementFamily and DistributedInstalledPlan.swift (unit 29/30). The mlx-swift-lm submodule bump (unit 29) is not visible. The routed-expert prior extracts the constants 128 and 8 and adds a pure string predicate on tensor names. The inventory fingerprint still pins tensor names and bytes, so there is no key, network or attestation exposure. The effect is on placement accuracy only.

The main behavior change is that a serial-prefill Gemma 4 layer-stage pipeline now defaults to 4 lanes (gemma4PipelineBatchLanes) instead of 1. Lookahead, private images, other adapters and an invalid override fall back to 1. Saved widths and the owner override still take precedence. Docs claim each lane is admitted against live memory on every rank, a cancelled lane retires alone, both owners bind the width into the load agreement (Gemma4BatchArithmeticAgreement), and shared expert dispatch keeps per-row bytes unchanged. The tests encode the defaults, the environment propagation and the lookahead fallback.

Relevant threats are availability and GPU memory (T-029, T-010, A-018), cross-request isolation and residual data (A-001, T-028), and prefix-cache scoping under concurrent lanes (T-041). No supplied evidence shows a regression. The memory admission code (QwenResidentRuntime.reserveLane, CBv2StageKVHost), the lane isolation code (Gemma4BatchDecodeScope, SwitchGLU.callAndWeightedReduceRows), the per-lane cacheSalt handling and the mlx-swift-lm submodule contents are not in the evidence. Their claims are unverified contracts, not findings.

Integration source replay was incomplete (omitted units), so unseen hunks are a coverage limit. A follow-up should confirm that the 4-lane default is enforced by live-memory admission on both ranks, that rows and caches do not mix across tenants, and that the submodule bump is reviewed separately.
